items.title: spans stick to their text across edits — on every `didChange`, the LSP shifts its cached diagnostics, inlay hints, semantic tokens, references and quick-fix spans by the edit's delta BEFORE the re-analysis lands, so nothing drifts while the developer types
items.body:
Today a span published before an edit stays at its old offset until the next analysis publishes new ones; between the keystroke and that publish (870 ms on a kolt leaf, 1.6 s with importers open; E121) every underline, hint and token sits one edit behind the text. The owner's hope 3: spans update position instantly on insert, sticking to their text, for diagnostics, inlay hints, rename, go-to-definition, Find References, quick fixes, semantic highlighting and the rest.

This is LSP-side bookkeeping, independent of compiler incrementality (every mature server does it): keep the last published results per document with the document version they were computed for; on `didChange`, map each span through the content changes (an edit before a span shifts it, an edit inside a span grows or truncates it, an edit after leaves it); republish the shifted set at once (diagnostics) or answer requests from it (hints, tokens, references) until the new analysis replaces it; semantic tokens use the delta protocol so the client does not repaint. Pin: a scripted edit above a diagnostic, the published range moves by the edit's length before any analysis runs (the counters prove none ran). Sizing M; vilan-lsp `document.rs`/`main.rs` (incr-47's `edited` plumbing is the hook).

items.title: the test suite analyses std once per process, not once per test — a workspace run is 9,777 tests in 21–32 min under load, and most of the compiler tests pay a cold std world (about 1.2 G instructions each) before their own program
items.body: The owner's hope 6: the suite runs much faster without losing quality. Where the time goes (measure first): M120 says an empty web program is 1.48 G of which 1.23 G is std; the inference, corpus, docs and LSP suites each analyse hundreds of small programs and most of that is std, repeated. incr-47's S1 gives the mechanism: a hot set covering the WHOLE package makes the stored prefix std-only, so one std world per (toolchain, std content, platform, prelude) can be built once per test binary and extended per test (`load_hot_modules`); the edit-replay differential already proves a served world equals a clean one. Doors: (a) the in-process std prefix shared by every test in a binary (the test harness's `Workspace` takes it); (b) nextest partitions and the slow tests' own fixes (the 4–6 `SLOW` tests); (c) a census of duplicate pins. Gate: wall time of `cargo nextest run --workspace -j 6` at load < 2 before and after, and the differential green with the shared prefix on. Blocked only for the cross-process form by M36 (6.15); the in-process form is not.
